overview.text: The differences between the adult female and male pelvis relate to function and body size.
overview.label: 8.3 Comparison of the Female and Male Pelvis

overview.text: The ischial tuberosities of females are also farther apart, which increases the size of the pelvic outlet.
overview.label: 8.3 Comparison of the Female and Male Pelvis

overview.text: Because of this increased pelvic width, the subpubic angle is larger in females (greater than 80 degrees) than it is in males (less than 70 degrees).
overview.label: 8.3 Comparison of the Female and Male Pelvis

overview.text: The female sacrum is wider, shorter, and less curved, and the sacral promontory projects less into the pelvic cavity, thus giving the female pelvic inlet (pelvic brim) a more rounded or oval shape compared to males.
overview.label: 8.3 Comparison of the Female and Male Pelvis

hip.text: The hip bone, or coxal bone, forms the pelvic girdle portion of the pelvis.
hip.label: 8.3 Hip Bone

hip.text: Each adult hip bone is formed by three separate bones that fuse together during the late teenage years.
hip.label: 8.3 Hip Bone

ilium.text: The ilium is the fan-like, superior region that forms the largest part of the hip bone.
ilium.label: 8.3 Hip Bone

ilium.text: This curved, superior margin of the ilium is the iliac crest.
ilium.label: 8.3 Ilium

ischium.text: The ischium forms the posteroinferior region of each hip bone.
ischium.label: 8.3 Hip Bone

ischium.text: The large, roughened area of the inferior ischium is the ischial tuberosity.
ischium.label: 8.3 Ischium

pubis.text: The pubis curves medially, where it joins to the pubis of the opposite hip bone at a specialized joint called the pubic symphysis.
pubis.label: 8.3 Hip Bone

pubis.text: The enlarged medial portion of the pubis is the pubic body.
pubis.label: 8.3 Pubis

sacrum.text: The female sacrum is wider, shorter, and less curved, and the sacral promontory projects less into the pelvic cavity, thus giving the female pelvic inlet (pelvic brim) a more rounded or oval shape compared to males.
sacrum.label: 8.3 Comparison of the Female and Male Pelvis

sacrum.text: The sacral promontory is the anterior lip of the superior base of the sacrum.
sacrum.label: 7.3 Sacrum and Coccyx

coccyx.text: Similarly, the coccyx, or tailbone, results from the fusion of four small coccygeal vertebrae.
coccyx.label: 7.3 Regions of the Vertebral Column

coccyx.text: It articulates with the inferior tip of the sacrum.
coccyx.label: 7.3 Sacrum and Coccyx

compare.text: In general, the bones of the male pelvis are thicker and heavier, adapted for support of the male’s heavier physical build and stronger muscles.
compare.label: 8.3 Comparison of the Female and Male Pelvis

compare.text: The greater sciatic notch of the male hip bone is narrower and deeper than the broader notch of females.
compare.label: 8.3 Comparison of the Female and Male Pelvis

compare.text: The lesser pelvic cavity of females is also wider and more shallow than the narrower, deeper, and tapering lesser pelvis of males.
compare.label: 8.3 Comparison of the Female and Male Pelvis
